question.text: Which of the following is a valid ground for withdrawal of an open offer under Regulation 23 of SAST?

answer.text: Deterioration in the financial condition of the target company
The acquirer's inability to arrange financing
A material adverse change in the target company's business
Death of the acquirer, where the acquirer is an individual

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Regulation 23 of the SAST Regulations, an open offer may be withdrawn only in limited circumstances: (i) statutory approvals disclosed in the detailed public statement / letter of offer are finally refused; (ii) death of the acquirer where the acquirer is a natural person; (iii) a condition of the acquisition agreement disclosed in the DPS/letter of offer is not met for reasons outside the acquirer's reasonable control, and the agreement is rescinded; or (iv) circumstances which, in SEBI's opinion, merit withdrawal. General financial difficulties, inability to arrange financing, or a material adverse change in the target's business are not listed grounds. The Trap: "Material adverse change" (MAC) is a common clause in private M&A agreements, but it is not a recognised withdrawal ground for an open offer under SAST. Note: Source - NISM-Series-IX Merchant Banking Certification Examination workbook (Jan 2026), p. 216.
